ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Gwen Ifill

code.originalText: Midpoint of combination treatment: blood counts, immune-related adverse event checks, neuropathy, and mood

text.paragraph: Review at the midpoint of combination treatment, on the day of cycle 4. [S]

Ms. Ifill returns on the day of her fourth cycle. Cycles 2 and 3 were given on schedule in the infusion center. Nausea lasts a day or two after each cycle and is controlled with ondansetron two or three times. For about two weeks she has had tingling in her toes that does not affect walking or balance. Her hair has thinned and she wears a wig. She has had no diarrhea, rash, cough, breathlessness or headache. She is tired for two or three days after each cycle and works from home on those days. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-04-28; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 71.8 kg; blood pressure 120/76, pulse 82
No leg swelling; calf circumferences unchanged
Pinprick slightly reduced over the toes; vibration sense and ankle reflexes present; strength normal; steady gait

Postmenopausal bleeding for three weeks, about eight years after her last period, in a woman of 60 who takes no hormone therapy: endometrial cancer must be excluded. Office endometrial biopsy taken today, transvaginal ultrasound this week, and gynecologic oncology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem; no symptom of her real illness was made public. Superseded by the diagnosis at the gynecologic oncology consultation.

Endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium, FIGO grade 2, mismatch repair deficient (loss of MLH1 and PMS2 staining), p53 wild-type pattern, on office endometrial biopsy, with enlarged right pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes on CT; surgical staging planned; synthetic modern detail linked to her publicly reported endometrial cancer
S — Synthetic histology, molecular result and extent; her family gave endometrial cancer as the cause of death (D), and nothing more about it was made public.

Metastatic endometrioid carcinoma in the right external iliac sentinel lymph node (9 mm deposit) and a left para-aortic lymph node (14 mm deposit), with the other nodes removed negative: FIGO 2023 stage IIIC2ii
S — Synthetic nodal disease found at surgical staging.
Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy from paclitaxel: tingling in the toes, grade 1 (sensory only, no effect on daily activities)
S — Synthetic common effect of paclitaxel.

list.item:
Endometrioid endometrial cancer, stage IIIC2ii, MMRd, on dostarlimab with carboplatin and paclitaxel (C54.1). Tolerating treatment. Counts allow cycle 4: neutrophils 2.1, platelets 196; hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL, mild anemia from chemotherapy without symptoms. Kidney and liver function are normal; magnesium 1.8 mg/dL. TSH 4.8 is just above range with a normal free T4 of 1.1: an early thyroid change to watch, which needs no treatment now. Morning cortisol 12.6 is normal. [S]
Cycle 4 today at full dose.
TSH and free T4 before each remaining cycle.
CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis two weeks after cycle 6.

Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, grade 1 (G62.0). Grade 1 sensory neuropathy from paclitaxel without functional effect. No medicine prevents it; the paclitaxel dose is reduced if it begins to interfere with daily activities (grade 2) or becomes painful. [S]
Continue paclitaxel at full dose with a check before each cycle.
Report trouble with buttons, writing or balance, or burning pain.
Duloxetine if it becomes painful.
